process_description: Object-centric event log capturing the item-level lifecycle of standard purchase orders subject to 3-way matching: PO item creation, goods receipt posting, and invoice receipt/verification, enabling reconciliation of PO, GR, and IR quantities/amounts per item.

activities.notes: EKKO/EKPO give the PO header/item attributes (incl. WEBRE flag confirming 3-way-match scope). EKPO has no creation timestamp of its own; CDHDR/CDPOS (OBJECTCLAS=EINKBELEG) supply the precise create event timestamp — EKKO.AEDAT is date-only and a fallback only.

EKBE rows with VGABE=1 are the goods-receipt events against the PO item; BELNR/GJAHR join to MKPF (header, reliable CPUDT/CPUTM) and MSEG (item, movement type BWART for distinguishing receipt vs reversal, e.g. 101 vs 102).

EKBE rows with VGABE=2 are the invoice-receipt events against the PO item; BELNR/GJAHR join to RBKP (header, CPUDT/CPUTM for ordering, STBLG flags reversed invoices as rework) and RSEG (line linking invoice back to EBELN+EBELP for the 3-way match).
Rework/exception activities: MSEG movement-type reversal pairs (e.g. 101/102) and RBKP.STBLG-populated invoices signal reversals that should be modeled as distinct events, not filtered out.

case_granularity_rationale: The use case explicitly asks for 'item-level granularity' and centers on 3-way match, which is inherently evaluated per PO line item (EBELN+EBELP) — quantities/amounts on a single item's GR and IR must reconcile against that same item's PO quantity/price. EKPO's own documented typical_role also flags EBELN+EBELP as the standard item-level case-notion grain for this exact analysis (consistent with BPI Challenge 2019-style P2P mining), and WEBRE (GR-based invoice verification / 3-way-match trigger) is an item-level flag, not a header-level one.

known_gaps.description: EKPO carries no native creation timestamp; without CDHDR/CDPOS logging enabled for object EINKBELEG, item-creation time degrades to EKKO.AEDAT, which is date-only and cannot support sub-day activity ordering.

EKKO.FRGKE only exposes the current overall release state, not a per-approver approval history; that trail (who approved what, when) is not available in standard P2P tables in this KB and would need workflow tables outside scope.

Standard P2P tables here show GR/IR events and amounts but do not directly expose invoice 'blocked for payment due to match variance' status — that requires FI blocking-reason fields not covered in this KB scope, so payment-block analysis is out of scope for this plan.

confidence_notes.topic: EKBE as unified GR/IR event source
confidence_notes.rationale: EKBE's VGABE field cleanly discriminates goods-receipt (1) vs invoice-receipt (2) rows per PO item, and its schema explicitly lists both as typical roles; this is the KB's documented richest source after CDHDR/CDPOS.
Directly grounded in the user's explicit 'item-level granularity' requirement and EKPO's own documented typical_role calling out EBELN+EBELP as the standard case grain for 3-way-match style analysis.

confidence_notes.topic: Use of CDHDR/CDPOS for PO-item creation timestamp
confidence_notes.rationale: The KB confirms CDHDR/CDPOS exist and are the right source per EKPO's own gotcha, but whether change-document logging is actually active for EINKBELEG in a given system is a data-availability assumption I can't verify from schema alone.

MSEG and RBKP schemas both flag reversal signals (BWART pairs, STBLG) as legitimate rework events per their gotchas, but the user's use case didn't explicitly ask for rework/exception modeling — included as a reasonable scope extension for a 3-way-match analysis, not a hard requirement.
